sourcedFrom: Weatherby® PUMP SHOTGUN PA459 OWNER'S MANUAL — Weatherby Pump Shotgun PA459 Owner's Manual, printed November 2009 (2009)
cleanIntro: The PA459 is a slide-action 12 gauge whose barrel is held by the magazine cap alone. It comes apart in a fixed order: hammer cocked and bolt closed, magazine cap off, barrel pushed forward off, forearm and slide forward off the magazine tube with the bolt riding on them, bolt lifted off the slide, then the trigger assembly out on its frame pin. Weatherby asks for a cleaning immediately after each use and periodically in storage.

steps.title: Safety button pushed left to right - that is SAFE
steps.action: The safety is a button at the rear of the trigger guard. Push it from left to right until it stops and stays. That is SAFE; pushed back through from right to left it is FIRE, and a red mark shows on the left of the trigger guard.
steps.prose: Fingers outside the trigger guard while you work it. If you can see red on the left side, the gun is on FIRE.
steps.quote: To engage the manual safety, push the safety button from left to right with your thumb or index finger until it stops and stays in place in the "SAFE" position.
steps.cite: Weatherby® PUMP SHOTGUN PA459 OWNER'S MANUAL — Weatherby Pump Shotgun PA459 Owner's Manual, printed November 2009 — MANUAL SAFETY OPERATION, printed p.6 (PDF p.7)

steps.title: Work the forearm until the magazine is empty
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction. Pull the forearm rearward to extract the shell in the chamber, push it forward to feed the next, and repeat until the magazine tube is empty.
steps.prose: If the forearm will not come back with the hammer cocked, the slide lock lever beside the trigger guard releases it - the book has you press it whenever you open the bolt. Count the shells out against what you loaded.
steps.quote: Pull the forearm rearward to extract any shell from the chamber.
steps.cite: Weatherby® PUMP SHOTGUN PA459 OWNER'S MANUAL — Weatherby Pump Shotgun PA459 Owner's Manual, printed November 2009 — UNLOADING THE SHOTGUN, printed p.13 (PDF p.14)

steps.title: Look: chamber empty, magazine empty
steps.action: With the bolt open, look into the chamber and the magazine and confirm there are no shells in either.
steps.prose: A look, not an assumption. A shell left on the shell latch or in the loading port is still a loaded gun.
steps.quote: Visually confirm that there are no shot shells remaining in the magazine or the chamber.
steps.cite: Weatherby® PUMP SHOTGUN PA459 OWNER'S MANUAL — Weatherby Pump Shotgun PA459 Owner's Manual, printed November 2009 — UNLOADING THE SHOTGUN, printed p.13 (PDF p.14)

steps.title: Forearm back then forward - hammer cocked, bolt closed
steps.action: Pull the forearm to the rear, which cocks the hammer, then push it all the way forward to close the bolt.
steps.prose: The hammer has to be cocked before the trigger assembly can come out later, and the barrel comes off with the bolt closed. This one stroke does both.
steps.quote: Pull forearm to rear then forward to make sure the hammer is cocked.
steps.cite: Weatherby® PUMP SHOTGUN PA459 OWNER'S MANUAL — Weatherby Pump Shotgun PA459 Owner's Manual, printed November 2009 — DISASSEMBLY OF TRIGGER ASSEMBLY FROM RECEIVER, printed p.14 (PDF p.15)

steps.title: Magazine cap off, counter-clockwise
steps.action: Unscrew the magazine cap at the front of the magazine tube, counter-clockwise, until it comes off.
steps.prose: The cap is the only thing holding the barrel on. Keep it somewhere you will find it.
steps.quote: Unscrew the magazine cap by turning it in a counter clock-wise direction until easily detached
steps.cite: Weatherby® PUMP SHOTGUN PA459 OWNER'S MANUAL — Weatherby Pump Shotgun PA459 Owner's Manual, printed November 2009 — DISASSEMBLY OF BARREL FROM RECEIVER, printed p.13 (PDF p.14)

steps.title: Barrel pushed forward off the receiver
steps.action: Grasp the barrel firmly and push it forward, toward the muzzle, until its tang is clear of the receiver ring, then lift it away.
steps.prose: Straight forward along the magazine tube. The barrel support ring slides off the end of the tube as the shank leaves the receiver.
steps.quote: Remove the barrel by grasping firmly and pushing forward (in the direction of the muzzle) until the barrel tang is clear of the receiver ring.
steps.cite: Weatherby® PUMP SHOTGUN PA459 OWNER'S MANUAL — Weatherby Pump Shotgun PA459 Owner's Manual, printed November 2009 — DISASSEMBLY OF BARREL FROM RECEIVER, printed p.13 (PDF p.14)

steps.title: Forearm and slide forward off the tube, bolt with them
steps.action: Slide the forearm assembly forward along the magazine tube until the bolt assembly clears the receiver.
steps.prose: The bolt rides out on the slide. Go slowly at the end so it does not drop off as it leaves the receiver.
steps.quote: Remove forearm by sliding the forearm assembly forward until the bolt assembly clears the receiver.
steps.cite: Weatherby® PUMP SHOTGUN PA459 OWNER'S MANUAL — Weatherby Pump Shotgun PA459 Owner's Manual, printed November 2009 — DISASSEMBLY OF BOLT FROM RECEIVER, printed p.14 (PDF p.15)

steps.title: Bolt lifted off the slide at the retainer pin
steps.action: Line the bolt up with the bolt retainer pin, then slide it forward and rearward while lifting it up until it comes off the slide.
steps.prose: It only lifts free where it lines up with the pin; anywhere else you are prying against it.
steps.quote: The bolt must be aligned with the bolt retainer pin. Slide the bolt forward and rearward while lifting up to detach the bolt from the slide
steps.cite: Weatherby® PUMP SHOTGUN PA459 OWNER'S MANUAL — Weatherby Pump Shotgun PA459 Owner's Manual, printed November 2009 — DISASSEMBLY OF BOLT FROM RECEIVER, printed p.14 (PDF p.15)

steps.title: Trigger frame pin out with a hammer and punch
steps.action: Safety on SAFE. With a hammer and punch, drive the trigger frame pin through the receiver until you can grasp it, then pull it out.
steps.prose: Drive it only until it can be gripped by hand; the rest comes out with your fingers.
steps.quote: With a hammer and punch push the trigger frame pin through the receiver (refer to Fig. 7) until the pin is out far enough to be grasped by hand, and remove the pin from the receiver.
steps.cite: Weatherby® PUMP SHOTGUN PA459 OWNER'S MANUAL — Weatherby Pump Shotgun PA459 Owner's Manual, printed November 2009 — DISASSEMBLY OF TRIGGER ASSEMBLY FROM RECEIVER, printed p.14 (PDF p.15)
steps.warn: Keep the safety in the “ON” (“SAFE”) position at all times while the trigger assembly is removed from the receiver.

steps.title: Trigger assembly forward, then straight out
steps.action: Pull the trigger assembly slightly forward, then straight out of the receiver.
steps.prose: Leave the trigger alone while the assembly is out of the gun - the hammer is cocked, and that is how it stays until the assembly is back in.
steps.quote: Pull the trigger assembly slightly forward and then straight out from the receiver.
steps.cite: Weatherby® PUMP SHOTGUN PA459 OWNER'S MANUAL — Weatherby Pump Shotgun PA459 Owner's Manual, printed November 2009 — DISASSEMBLY OF TRIGGER ASSEMBLY FROM RECEIVER, printed p.14 (PDF p.15)
steps.warn: Do not pull the trigger while the trigger assembly is outside of the receiver.

steps.title: Choke tube out, counter-clockwise
steps.action: Grasp the choke tube with fingers or soft-jawed pliers and turn it counter-clockwise until it comes out of the muzzle.
steps.prose: Soft jaws only. It goes back in clockwise, snug and no tighter.
steps.quote: Turn the choke tube counter-clockwise until it emerges from the muzzle.
steps.cite: Weatherby® PUMP SHOTGUN PA459 OWNER'S MANUAL — Weatherby Pump Shotgun PA459 Owner's Manual, printed November 2009 — REMOVING CHOKE TUBE, printed p.8 (PDF p.9)

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Barrel, choke tube, forearm and slide, bolt and trigger assembly are out. The book stops here.
steps.prose: Anything further is for a Weatherby Authorized Service Center or a gunsmith, in the book's own words.
steps.quote: Further disassembly of the shotgun is not recommended. If further disassembly is required, contact a Weatherby Authorized Service Center or your local gunsmith.
steps.cite: Weatherby® PUMP SHOTGUN PA459 OWNER'S MANUAL — Weatherby Pump Shotgun PA459 Owner's Manual, printed November 2009 — REMOVAL OF MAGAZINE BLOCKER, printed p.15 (PDF p.16)

steps.title: Bore brushed from the chamber end, choke threads twisted
steps.action: Wet a bore brush with solvent and push it all the way through the bore several times from the chamber end. Then put it into the muzzle only as far as the choke tube threads and twist it several times.
steps.prose: Chamber end first, always. Then patches from the chamber end until one comes out clean.
steps.quote: Insert the brush into the muzzle of the barrel only far enough to encounter the threads for the choke tube, and twist it several times.
steps.cite: Weatherby® PUMP SHOTGUN PA459 OWNER'S MANUAL — Weatherby Pump Shotgun PA459 Owner's Manual, printed November 2009 — CLEANING THE BORE, printed p.15 (PDF p.16)

steps.title: Oiled patch, then a dry one - no oil left in the bore
steps.action: Push a lubricant-soaked patch through from the chamber end, then a dry clean patch to take off the excess.
steps.prose: The dry patch is the point. The book warns that excess oil in the bore or chamber can raise chamber pressure or partly obstruct the bore.
steps.quote: Insert a dry, clean patch into the cleaning rod tip and push it through the bore from the chamber end, to remove excess lubricant.
steps.cite: Weatherby® PUMP SHOTGUN PA459 OWNER'S MANUAL — Weatherby Pump Shotgun PA459 Owner's Manual, printed November 2009 — CLEANING THE BORE, printed p.16 (PDF p.17)
steps.warn: BE SURE ALL EXCESS LUBRICANT HAS BEEN REMOVED.

steps.title: Choke tube brushed and patched through
steps.action: Brush the choke tube through with solvent, patch it until clean, oil it, then a dry patch. Wipe the outside and threads with solvent, dry them, and leave a light coat of oil.
steps.prose: A toothbrush gets the threads. Light oil on the threads, wiped back.
steps.quote: Push the brush all the way through the choke tube several times.
steps.cite: Weatherby® PUMP SHOTGUN PA459 OWNER'S MANUAL — Weatherby Pump Shotgun PA459 Owner's Manual, printed November 2009 — CLEANING CHOKE TUBES, printed p.16 (PDF p.17)

steps.title: Receiver and bolt: solvent, dry, a light coat of oil
steps.action: Clean the inside and outside of the receiver and the bolt assembly with solvent on a small lint-free cloth, dry them thoroughly, then a light coat of oil on every accessible surface.
steps.prose: A clean toothbrush reaches the recesses of the bolt.
steps.quote: Using a small lint-free cloth, clean the inside and outside of the bolt assembly with gun-cleaning solvent; and dry thoroughly with a clean cloth.
steps.cite: Weatherby® PUMP SHOTGUN PA459 OWNER'S MANUAL — Weatherby Pump Shotgun PA459 Owner's Manual, printed November 2009 — CLEANING THE BOLT, printed p.17 (PDF p.18)

steps.title: Slide and forearm assembly, then the magazine tube outside
steps.action: Clean the slide and forearm assembly inside and out with solvent and dry it; then the outside of the magazine tube. A light coat of oil on both.
steps.prose: The slide rides on the outside of the magazine tube, so that outer surface is the one that matters.
steps.quote: Using a lint-free cloth, clean the outside of the magazine tube with gun-cleaning solvent; and dry thoroughly with a clean cloth.
steps.cite: Weatherby® PUMP SHOTGUN PA459 OWNER'S MANUAL — Weatherby Pump Shotgun PA459 Owner's Manual, printed November 2009 — CLEANING THE MAGAZINE, printed p.17 (PDF p.18)

steps.title: Trigger assembly: brushed on top, dried, trigger left alone
steps.action: Wipe the outside of the trigger assembly, brush the top of the mechanism with solvent on a clean toothbrush, then dry every exposed part thoroughly.
steps.prose: Hammer cocked and safety on SAFE the whole time it is out of the receiver.
steps.quote: Using a small lint-free cloth, clean the outside of the trigger assembly and with a clean toothbrush, brush the top surface of the trigger assembly mechanism with gun-cleaning solvent.
steps.cite: Weatherby® PUMP SHOTGUN PA459 OWNER'S MANUAL — Weatherby Pump Shotgun PA459 Owner's Manual, printed November 2009 — CLEANING THE TRIGGER ASSEMBLY, printed p.17 (PDF p.18)
steps.warn: Do not pull the trigger while the trigger assembly is outside of the receiver.

steps.title: Metal dried, then oiled and wiped
steps.action: After a thorough cleaning, let all metal parts dry for 2-3 hours at room temperature, then oil them and wipe off the excess. Wipe the forearm and buttstock with a clean dry cloth.
steps.prose: Wet weather: let the wood dry thoroughly before the gun goes away.
steps.quote: allow 2-3 hours at room temperature for all metal parts to dry completely.
steps.cite: Weatherby® PUMP SHOTGUN PA459 OWNER'S MANUAL — Weatherby Pump Shotgun PA459 Owner's Manual, printed November 2009 — RUST PREVENTION AND REMOVAL, printed p.17 (PDF p.18)

deepAbsentReason: The PA459 book ends at field disassembly. After the barrel, bolt, trigger assembly, choke tube and magazine blocker it says further disassembly of the shotgun is not recommended and sends it to a Weatherby Authorized Service Center or a local gunsmith (printed p.15). Everything the book publishes is walked in the field strip; nothing deeper is published, so nothing deeper is walked.

cleaning.name: BARREL & BORE
tasks: Solvent on a bore brush, pushed through several times from the chamber end
Brush into the muzzle only as far as the choke threads, and twisted
Patches from the chamber end until one comes out clean
Solvent wiped out of the muzzle and choke tube threads
Oiled patch, then a dry patch, from the chamber end
Light oil on the choke tube threads and muzzle
Outside of barrel, rib and barrel ring: solvent, dry, light oil
⛔ Never leave excess lubricant in the bore or chamber

cleaning.name: CHOKE TUBE
tasks: Brushed through with solvent, then patched until clean
Oiled patch, then a dry patch
Outside and threads wiped with solvent, dried, a light coat of oil
Do not over-tighten it going back in

cleaning.name: RECEIVER & BOLT
tasks: Receiver inside and out with solvent, dried, a light coat of oil
Bolt assembly inside and out with solvent, a toothbrush in the recesses, dried, a light coat of oil

cleaning.name: SLIDE, FOREARM & MAGAZINE TUBE
tasks: Slide and forearm assembly inside and out with solvent, dried, a light coat of oil
Outside of the magazine tube with solvent, dried, a light coat of oil

cleaning.name: TRIGGER ASSEMBLY
tasks: Outside wiped; top of the mechanism brushed with solvent
All exposed parts dried thoroughly
Do not pull the trigger while the trigger assembly is out of the receiver

cleaning.name: STOCK & RUST
tasks: Forearm and buttstock wiped with a clean dry cloth
Metal left 2-3 hours to dry, then oiled and wiped
Do not store it in a leather case, scabbard or foam-lined case

reassembly: No ammunition on the bench. Safety on SAFE; hammer still cocked.
Trigger assembly: push it into the receiver until flush with the bottom, push it rearward to line up the pin holes, and press the trigger frame pin in until flush with the side of the receiver.
Bolt onto the slide and forearm assembly.
Slide's tube over the magazine tube; move the slide toward the receiver, lining the bolt up as it enters, and slide the bolt in.
Barrel: check the chamber and bore are clear and clean. Move the forearm forward until the bolt sticks out slightly from the front of the receiver, with the bolt forward on the slide.
Line the barrel shank up with the bolt and the barrel support ring with the magazine tube; push the shank in until the barrel stops against the receiver.
Magazine cap on, clockwise, until seated.
Choke tube in clockwise, snug - do not over-tighten.
Function check before any live ammunition.
fncheck: The book publishes no separate function check. Muzzle in a safe direction, chamber and magazine proved empty. Work the action: press the slide lock lever and pull the forearm fully back, then push it fully forward - it should travel freely and close. Move the safety between SAFE and FIRE and back: it should stop and stay in each position, with the red mark showing on the left of the trigger guard on FIRE. To store the gun assembled, the book has you release the hammer spring: bolt closed, gun proved empty, muzzle safe, pull the trigger. If anything binds or does not behave as described, take it to a Weatherby Authorized Service Center.
